extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing interim suspension of a registered practitioner under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), including notice, proof requirements, referral to a hearing officer, filing deadlines, publication, and obligations during and for reinstatement from suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for interim suspension: conviction of a serious crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension of a practitioner may be ordered where there is proof that Respondent committed a serious crime; this action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.25. The Notice recited certified copies of an 'Abstract of Judgment - Prison Commitment' and 'Felony Sentencing Minutes' showing Respondent's felony conviction of Grand Theft Over $400 (Cal. Penal Code 487(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified court records demonstrating a felony conviction (e.g., Abstract of Judgment, sentencing minutes) may serve as proof supporting interim suspension. The example on the page: conviction by plea to grand theft predicated on withdrawals from a client trust account and subsequent sentencing (one year and four months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must mail a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25' informing the respondent of the Complaint and requesting information; the Notice directed Respondent to file, within 40 days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent is afforded a 40-day period to file a response that raises a genuine issue of material fact. Failure to file such a response permits a determination that no genuine issue of material fact exists and supports interim suspension. The document demonstrates that no response was filed and the Director accordingly determined there was no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination standard: no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.25(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a timely response or does not raise a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), the Director may determine that no genuine issue of material fact exists and that interim suspension and referral for formal proceedings are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states two determinations: (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b) and (2) interim suspension and referral of the Complaint to a hearing officer is appropriate. Non-response is shown as a basis for making this determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to a hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Where interim suspension is ordered under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), the Complaint shall be referred to the hearing officer identified in the Complaint for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral triggers institution of formal disciplinary proceedings before the specified hearing officer; the Final Order specifically sends the Complaint to the hearing officer named in the Complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a written answer to the Complaint within thirty (30) days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order requires that, within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, Respondent's written answer to the Complaint shall be filed with the hearing officer and a copy of the answer shall be served on the OED Director in accordance with the instructions set out in the Complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents must meet the 30-day deadline for filing an answer with the hearing officer and must serve the OED Director as instructed in the Complaint. The Order makes this a mandatory procedural step following interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is ordered to publish the Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette and to make disciplinary decisions regarding practitioners available at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspensions are publicly announced; publication in the Official Gazette and posting in the OED Reading Room are the mechanisms used. The notice text (including respondent name, registration number, crime, and sentence) is to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to USPTO employees, interested departments/agencies/courts, and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to 1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; 2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and 3) appropriate authorities of any State in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED must disseminate the suspension information to internal USPTO personnel and external authorities and courts, and to state bar authorities where the respondent is admitted, ensuring broad notification of disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during suspension: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order directs Respondent to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the text does not reproduce § 11.58, the citation imposes the procedural and ethical obligations specified there (e.g., notification to clients, disposition of client files, trust account handling). Respondents must consult § 11.58 to meet duties during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures: compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order notifies Respondent that they must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(e) should they seek reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement from an interim suspension requires satisfaction of the procedures and standards set out in § 11.25(e). The Order references this as the path for seeking reinstatement; practitioners must follow the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof/service methods and certificate of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service stating that the Final Order and a copy of the Disciplinary Complaint were mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent, who is incarcerated, via a State official able to personally present documents to Respondent (identifying the correctional counselor and address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a respondent is incarcerated, service may be effected via a State official who can personally present documents; the Order demonstrates use of first-class certified mail with return receipt and identification of the person receiving service on behalf of the incarcerated respondent. Maintain proof of mailing/receipt as part of the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of criminal record details as factual basis in the Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice sets out factual details underlying the criminal conviction (e.g., withdrawal of more than $13,000 from a client trust account and use for personal expenses; plea to one felony count after multiple charges; sentence imposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices may include factual summaries of the conduct underlying the criminal conviction to inform the public and the bar of the basis for interim suspension. Such factual recitals can be relied upon in the Director's determination absent a successful response raising a genuine issue.
